summary: Fix five colours early and deploy cheap party creatures so [[Tazri, Beacon of Unity]] costs as little as {W}. Use her activated dig to refuel the party every turn, then attack with anthems, double strike and extra combats behind [[Grand Abolisher]] or [[Heroic Intervention]].

phases.goal: fix five colours and land 1-2 cheap party creatures
cast Tazri cheap off the party discount and start digging
attack with anthems, double strike and extra combats behind protection

engine.title: Party count
flow: [[Changeling Outcast]] and [[Chomping Changeling]] count as every creature type
[[Tazri, Beacon of Unity]] costs {1} less per creature in your party
A full Cleric/Rogue/Warrior/Wizard party drops her to {W}

engine.title: Karlach + Blade Historian
flow: Attack with a wide board
[[Karlach, Fury of Avernus]] untaps all attackers and grants first strike, adding a second combat phase
[[Blade Historian]] grants every attacker double strike
Two combats, each with two damage steps
engine.note: Karlach does not have to be among the attacking creatures (Scryfall ruling), so keep her home as a value engine, not a combat risk.

engine.title: Najeela + Warriors
flow: Every changeling and every [[Springleaf Parade]] token is a Warrior
[[Najeela, the Blade-Blossom]] makes a tapped, attacking 1/1 Warrior token whenever a Warrior attacks
In the end-of-combat step, pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} to untap all attackers, grant trample/lifelink/haste, and add another combat
engine.note: Najeela's own tokens were never declared as attacking creatures, so they do not re-trigger Najeela, Ingris Stingerquill or Harper Recruiter (Scryfall ruling).

engine.title: Tazri's dig
flow: Activate {2/U}{2/B}{2/R}{2/G} at any time, no timing restriction
Look at the top six cards of your library
Take up to two Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, Wizard and/or Ally cards into hand

winConditions.name: Full-party alpha
flow: Full party assembled, 5+ creatures ready to attack
[[Grand Abolisher]] stops instant-speed answers during your turn
Attack: [[Blade Historian]] grants double strike to every attacker
[[Karlach, Fury of Avernus]] untaps attackers and adds a second combat phase
[[Najeela, the Blade-Blossom]] makes more Warrior tokens off each attack to refuel
winConditions.damage: 5+ attackers x double strike x 2 combat phases, usually lethal to one opponent

winConditions.name: Najeela + Springleaf Parade infinite combats
flow: [[Springleaf Parade]] tokens can tap for any colour of mana
Attack with 5+ creature tokens
Pay the first {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} from lands or tokens that stayed home
[[Najeela, the Blade-Blossom]] untaps all attackers, gives haste, adds a combat
Tap 5 untapped attacking tokens for the next {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}; repeat
Each Warrior attacking in the next combat makes another token
winConditions.damage: loops until every opponent is dead
winConditions.turn: late game, with 5+ attacking creature tokens and a first {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} from lands or tokens that did not attack (attacking tokens are tapped, and new ones need haste, CR 302.6; pilot guide rank 3)

winConditions.name: Ping per attacker
flow: Attack with a wide board
[[Ingris Stingerquill]] deals 1 damage to each opponent per attacking creature
[[Burakos, Party Leader]] makes the defending player lose X life and makes X Treasures, X = your party size
winConditions.damage: attackers x 1 (Ingris) plus party size (Burakos) per combat, doubling with Karlach's second combat

swaps.reason: Blade Historian grants every attacker double strike while it is on the battlefield. Concerted Defense is a one-shot counterspell that only taxes a noncreature spell, and misses creature spells entirely.
swaps.quoteOut: Counter target noncreature spell unless its controller pays {1} plus an additional {1} for each creature in your party.
swaps.quoteIn: Attacking creatures you control have double strike.

swaps.reason: Springleaf Parade's tokens, plus Najeela's untap-and-haste, build toward infinite combats. Bar the Gate is a one-shot counterspell on a creature or walker spell with no lasting board presence.
swaps.quoteOut: Counter target creature or planeswalker spell. Venture into the dungeon.
swaps.quoteIn: Creature tokens you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."

swaps.reason: Generous Gift is an instant answer to any permanent, land or otherwise. Solemn Doomguide is a 5-MV Cleric whose unearth only helps creature cards already in the graveyard.
swaps.quoteOut: Each creature card in your graveyard that's a Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and/or Wizard has unearth {1}{B}.
swaps.quoteIn: Destroy target permanent. Its controller creates a 3/3 green Elephant creature token.

swaps.reason: Infernal Grasp is unconditional creature removal for two mana. Acererak never stays on the battlefield: its own enter trigger returns it to hand unless you've completed Tomb of Annihilation.
swaps.quoteOut: When Acererak enters, if you haven't completed Tomb of Annihilation, return Acererak to its owner's hand and venture into the dungeon.
swaps.quoteIn: Destroy target creature. You lose 2 life.

swaps.reason: Grand Abolisher is a Cleric that locks out instant-speed answers on your alpha turn. Multiclass Baldric only prevents damage to the single equipped creature, and needs a full party to even do that.
swaps.quoteOut: As long as you have a full party, prevent all damage that would be dealt to equipped creature.
swaps.quoteIn: During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments.

swaps.reason: With 10 basics in the list, Land Tax refuels three basics to hand most upkeeps it is behind on lands. Yuan-Ti Malison is a 2/1 Rogue whose evasion only works while it attacks alone.
swaps.quoteOut: This creature can't be blocked as long as it's attacking alone.
swaps.quoteIn: At the beginning of your upkeep, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may search your library for up to three basic land cards, reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle.

swaps.reason: Twilight Prophet is a recurring Vampire Cleric that drains and draws every upkeep once you have the city's blessing. You Find a Cursed Idol is a one-shot modal sorcery, and Chomping Changeling already covers its artifact/enchantment removal mode.
swaps.quoteOut: Steal Its Eyes — Create a Treasure token and venture into the dungeon.
swaps.quoteIn: At the beginning of your upkeep, if you have the city's blessing, reveal the top card of your library and put it into your hand. Each opponent loses X life and you gain X life, where X is that card's mana value.

swaps.reason: The Destined Thief loots when your creatures deal combat damage to a player (draws three instead with a full party), can't be blocked itself, and for {U} and a tap makes another creature unblockable. Thwart the Grave is a party-discounted reanimation spell with no self-mill to feed it.
swaps.quoteOut: Return target creature card and up to one target Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, or Wizard creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield.
swaps.quoteIn: Whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to one or more players, draw a card, then discard a card. If you have a full party, instead draw three cards.

swaps.reason: Putrefy is unconditional artifact or creature removal that can't be regenerated. Shadowheart's draw engine costs a creature sacrifice every activation, which this deck would rather keep attacking with. The party loses a Cleric, but the removal is worth it.
swaps.quoteOut: {1}{B}, {T}, Sacrifice another creature: Draw X cards, where X is that creature's power.
swaps.quoteIn: Destroy target artifact or creature. It can't be regenerated.

swaps.reason: Kamiz makes an attacker unblockable and connives on every attack, Rogue for Rogue. Safana makes one Treasure per end step, and only while you hold the initiative.
swaps.quoteOut: At the beginning of your end step, if you have the initiative, create a Treasure token.
swaps.quoteIn: Whenever you attack, target attacking creature can't be blocked this turn. It connives.

swaps.reason: Mangara is a lifelink Cleric that draws off wide attacks and off an opponent's second spell each turn. Hama Pashar is a Wizard whose only text doubles dungeon room triggers, which this pass removed 7 venture/initiative cards' worth of support for.
swaps.quoteOut: Room abilities of dungeons you own trigger an additional time.
swaps.quoteIn: Whenever an opponent attacks with creatures, if two or more of those creatures are attacking you and/or planeswalkers you control, draw a card.

swaps.reason: Ingris pings every opponent for 1 per attacker, and its {4} makes a Wizard Soldier token and gives your creatures haste, a direct payoff for Najeela and Karlach's extra combats. REFUTE.md's original pairing was Keen Duelist for this slot, but its missed-swap pass found Ingris beats Keen Duelist too: Keen Duelist's draw is symmetric, feeding the targeted opponent a card as well. Feywild Caretaker is a 5-drop that takes the initiative and then makes one 1/1 flyer per end step while you keep it.
swaps.quoteOut: At the beginning of your end step, if you have the initiative, create a 1/1 blue Faerie Dragon creature token with flying.
swaps.quoteIn: Whenever a creature you control attacks, that creature deals 1 damage to each opponent.
swaps.evidence: REFUTE.md Tazri swap #12 and section 5 missed swap #2

swaps.reason: Weathered Wayfarer fetches any land to hand once an opponent is ahead on lands, which this five-colour manabase needs. Varis is an Elf Ranger, not a party type, and its venture only triggers once per turn off any creature or walker cast.
swaps.quoteOut: Whenever you cast a creature or planeswalker spell, venture into the dungeon. This ability triggers only once each turn.

swaps.quoteIn: Skulk (This creature can't be blocked by creatures with greater power.) This creature enters with X +1/+1 counters on it. At the beginning of your upkeep, if this creature has one or more +1/+1 counters on it, you may remove a +1/+1 counter from it. If you do, draw a card.

swaps.reason: Chomping Changeling is every creature type (always a party hit) and destroys an artifact or enchantment on entry, covering attack-tax enchantments like Ghostly Prison. Triumphant Adventurer is a Human Knight, not a party type.
swaps.quoteOut: During your turn, this creature has first strike. Whenever this creature attacks, venture into the dungeon.

swaps.quoteOut: Other creatures you control get +1/+1 as long as you've completed a dungeon.

keepers.why: Its ruling: lands simply put onto the battlefield tapped (Farseek, Kodama's Reach, the Courtyard/Hideout fetches) enter untapped, and self-tapping lands (tri-lands, a shock you don't pay 2 life for) can enter untapped because you choose the order of the two effects.

It is symmetric (each player keeps up to one Cleric, Rogue, Warrior and Wizard), so it hurts the go-wide board too. It earns its slot when the board is already against you: you keep a full party of four, while opponents whose creatures are not party types keep fewer. Never cast it while ahead on board (pilot guide).

It tutors any card to hand; with a full party it then casts a spell of mana value 4 or less from hand for free (the tutored card may be that spell). It most often finds Blade Historian, Grand Abolisher or Destined Warrior, not the whole combo, since the ruling confirms the free cast happens on resolution and X must be 0 (no free Springleaf Parade).

Looks like a plain 3-mana flyer, but her full-party ability can be pointed at a mana rock or the best blocker on the alpha turn, and she sacrifices herself for hexproof or indestructible when the board is under pressure.

A mana sink that only shines with the Springleaf Parade token army; at X=0 it kills your own board, since it overwrites base power and toughness to 0/0 (Scryfall ruling). Activate after blocks, with X high enough that Tazri (4/6) and Zagras (4/4) do not shrink.

keep: 3+ lands including a W source plus one other colour
at least 1 ramp or fixing piece (Farseek, Nature's Lore, Weathered Wayfarer, a rock)
at least 2 party creatures at mana value 3 or less
one party creature plus Tazri's dig mana is acceptable, since Tazri is free card flow from the command zone
mulligan: no white source: Tazri, Grand Abolisher and Stick Together all strand (Blade Historian's hybrid cost can be paid with red)
6+ lands and land-fetch spells with zero creatures
two tapped lands and nothing castable before T4
a hand of only 4+ MV party payoffs with no mana fixing

pilotRules: Activate Tazri's dig at the end of an opponent's turn, before yours; it has no timing restriction.
Fill missing party slots with the dig before digging for Najeela, Karlach or Blade Historian.
Commit 4-5 bodies to the board, but keep 1-2 party creatures in hand against a sweeper; Tazri's dig rebuilds the rest.

Attack order: combat triggers resolve, then everything except Najeela/Karlach/Ingris attacks, then Najeela's tokens, then blocks, then Mirror Entity's X, then damage, then Najeela's end-of-combat activation.
Never tap a Parade or Najeela token made this turn for mana without haste (CR 302.6).
Hold Heroic Intervention or Selfless Spirit until the board is fully committed, then fire it against a destroy-based wipe.
Use Grand Abolisher only on your own turn; it does nothing to protect against instant-speed answers on an opponent's turn.

Mangara, the Diplomat trades Hama Pashar's Wizard slot for a Cleric; keep casting Mangara into open mana anyway: the extra draws from wide attacks and from punishing a second spell matter more than the dungeon package this list cut.
